body: blocked: waits for #916 (the solidcore STEP bench).

Same rule as #916: the solidcore crates are pinned by `rev` to the owner's fork https://github.com/NeoTech/solidcore, each pinned commit tagged `camcraft-pin-<date>` there. This replaces "git pin on upstream" wherever this issue says it.

The maintainer asked for this work on 2026-11-19. His words: "So then its time to throw out stepio from truck and finalize the switch to solidcore".

Label changes:

- `P6` becomes `P4`, because the maintainer asked for the work in his own words.
- `blocked` is removed. The block was #916 (the solidcore STEP bench). #916 is closed and shipped in v0.19.0. Nothing else blocks this issue.

Scope, as the maintainer set it today:

- The STEP import of the app goes through the solidcore importer behind the kernel seam.
- `truck-stepio` and `ruststep` leave `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`. truck stays only where code that is not STEP import needs it. This replaces "`truck-*` leaves" in the issue body.
- The import behaviour in the UI and the CLI stays: the error text, the refusal of corrupt input, and no crash.
- The solidcore pin moves to `2016386442dfee3b2a0c3a1bfdd4017c5254dac8` in this work (#2781).
- #2780 (a legal file with a twisted B-spline flank is refused) must close with this switch if the new importer reads such a face. A STEP fixture that we make ourselves confirms it.

The work starts after the gate of PR #2773 and the process bump. Only one local build runs at a time.

Priority is P3 by the maintainer's order. The reason is a defect: the truck STEP importer refuses legal files (see #2780). The switch to solidcore is the fix. This follows the P1-P3 rule, with no exception.

Maintainer direction (relayed by the main session, 2026-11-19): the app uses solidcore for all STEP reading. No second STEP path stays.

Scope that this adds to the issue:

- Port each reader that uses `ruststep` to the `solidcore-step` parser. These are the five readers outside the importer:
  - `step_csys.rs` (the tool-body coordinate reader, used by the `tool_body*` commands)
  - `step_closed.rs`
  - `step_diag.rs`
  - `step_units.rs`
  - `step_depth.rs`
- Remove `truck-stepio` and `ruststep` fully from each `Cargo.toml` and from `Cargo.lock`. Remove the `[patch.crates-io]` entry for `ruststep` too.
- Keep `truck` only where code that does not read STEP needs it.
- Keep the import behaviour of the UI and the CLI: the error text, the refusal on corrupt input, no crash and no hang.

Split rule:

- If the work is too large for one PR, the worker splits it into stacked PRs.
- The PRs are worked one at a time. Each PR has its own gate.
- Each part gets a sub-issue under this issue, with `P3`. The sub-issues are worked in the bug lane.

The solidcore pin move of #2781 stays a part of this work. #2780 closes with it only if a fixture that we make ourselves confirms the result.

claimed: issue-worker-max (Opus) · 2026-11-19T17:28Z · worktree/branch issue-917 / issue/917-solidcore-step · plan: solidcore straight through for all STEP reading; truck-stepio and ruststep removed; #2781 pin move folded in

The worker split the work into three stacked PRs. They are worked one at a time, each with its own gate.

1. Part 1, branch `issue/917-solidcore-step` (`Refs #917`): the solidcore pin move of #2781, the STEP importer through `camcraft_geometry::step` to the kernel, the removal of the truck helper modules from the app. The code is written. It is not built yet: only one build runs on the machine at a time.
2. Part 2, #2789: the tool coordinate reader, the units reader and the depth check use the `solidcore-step` parser. `ruststep` leaves the app.
3. Part 3, #2790: `truck-stepio` and `ruststep` leave the workspace and the kernel bench. Its PR closes this issue.

Open risk for part 1: at the old pin, solidcore refused four tracked fixtures (`fig8.step`, `fillet_corner.step`, `bar_cross_holes.step`, `bspline_discontinuous.step`). The first build shows if the new pin reads them. If it does not, part 1 cannot merge as planned, and the finding comes here.

Finding from the first build of part 1: the new solidcore pin (`2016386442dfee3b2a0c3a1bfdd4017c5254dac8`) refuses three tracked fixtures that the truck importer reads. Part 1 is stopped. No test was weakened and no fixture was changed.

Readings from the kernel bench (`crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement.rs`, debug):

| Fixture | solidcore at the new pin | truck |
|---|---|---|
| `fig8.step` | refused at read: pcurves failed on 1 of 30 faces: `not supported yet: no exact pcurve of a NURBS on a spline surface` | reads, V=136543.72 |
| `fillet_corner.step` | refused at read: pcurves failed on 1 of 10 faces, same reason | reads, V=20651.68 |
| `bar_cross_holes.step` | refused at read: pcurves failed on 3 of 7 faces: `no exact pcurve of a B-spline on a spline surface` | reads, V=45816.21 |
| `bspline_discontinuous.step` | refused (pcurve of a line on a spline surface) | refused too: no change |
| `twisted_flank.step` (our own fixture for #2780) | reads, 1 solid, V=8000.000000, watertight | open shell, V=0 |
| `Milling-test.step`, `Milling-test-inch.step` | the bounding box now agrees (#939) | - |

Each other tracked fixture keeps its verdict.

Result: the switch of the app importer changes three fixtures from import to refusal. That is a regression, so part 1 cannot merge as planned. The cause is in solidcore: it has no exact pcurve of a NURBS or B-spline curve on a spline surface.

The new pin needs one build fix in the kernel: `brep::Surface` has a new `Blend` variant (`crates/kernel/src/mesh_bound.rs`, `mesh_deviation.rs`).

Held work: branch `issue/917-solidcore-step`, commit 776ba8b76548e3094a13534a0325332c69473039. It is not gated and has no PR.

The decision how to continue is with the maintainer. #2789 and #2790 wait for it.

Cause of the three refusals, from the pinned solidcore source (worker reading, not built):

- solidcore makes an exact pcurve only in closed form: a curve on a plane, a circle about an axis, a ruling line, and on a spline face only a straight (u,v) line. `crates/solidcore/src/eval/pcurve.rs` says that nothing is fitted. This is an intended limit, not a defect.
- Each refused face is on a B-spline or NURBS surface, and the failing edge is a free-form 3D curve on that face. truck fitted a pcurve there and imported the file.
- solidcore has a seam for this: `solidcore-step` has `read_solids_with(ex, &dyn Trims)`, and `solidcore_ops::pcurve::Trims` is a kernel that makes the pcurves that have no closed form. Only tests implement `Trims`. The default read passes no `Trims`, so these faces are refused.
- The upstream repository has no issue list and no branch for this.

Two ways to make the three fixtures read through solidcore:

1. solidcore ships a production `Trims` kernel that projects or fits the pcurve and checks it by a lift to 3D.
2. `camcraft-kernel` implements `Trims` and calls `read_solids_with`.

The two ways use a fitted pcurve. That is a design decision for the maintainer.

Part that can stand alone now, without the importer switch (kernel crate only): the pin move of #2781, the `Blend` arms, the new bench verdicts, our two `twisted_flank` fixtures, and a kernel test that pins the read at V=8000. Risk that is not verified by a build: the app fixture walkers still use truck, and truck reads `twisted_flank.step` as an open shell.

Held branch: `issue/917-solidcore-step` at 776ba8b76548e3094a13534a0325332c69473039 (pushed, no PR).
